resources.string: Your own copy of the game, rebuilt to run natively on this phone.
Recompia turns your own copy of the game into a program that runs natively on this phone. The game is built here, on this phone, from your files.

This happens when the update is dumped without the base game’s files under it, or when copying the romfs folder stopped early. In the game (pause menu, Settings, Display) the resolution and the upscaler change at once; on a phone with less than 12 GB of memory a higher resolution than the one the game started with waits for the next start. The other rows take effect the next time the game starts.
Lowers the resolution while the phone cannot keep the frame rate, and raises it back up to the one above.
SGSR sharpens the enlarged 3D picture; menus and text stay sharp.
New ways of playing: switch each one on or off here. They take effect the next time the game starts, and they need the game built with this version (Set up again once after an update).
Hide when a controller is connected
The layout itself is edited in the game: open the overlay menu and choose Edit layout.
The settings files cannot be read. Allow storage access first.
Sort button in the bag and containers
Sort each time the bag opens
Save button in the pause menu
Abilities and tools aim where the camera looks instead of where your character faces, and your character turns to the target when the ability starts.
Adds an Items tab to the game’s Settings screen where you change how many of an item in your bag you hold. Off during Link Play. Back up your save first.
Experimental. Visitors and temporary spawns share the game’s 50 slots with your residents, so a high number leaves them less room.

Each tab has 3 pages (60 slots) and uses one of the island’s 256 big box spots. At 6 tabs (360 slots), about the first 42 big boxes placed get every tab. Later boxes get fewer or none. At 1, only the box itself is enabled. Tabs with items stay available if you lower the limit. Extra tabs are off during Link Play. Items stay saved.

Optional: a game library built on a PC
An Android game library built on a PC (libpkpgame.so) goes to Recompia/build on the phone (/sdcard/Recompia/build/libpkpgame.so): the Build step finds it there, checks it and offers to use it.
Lower is faster; shadow edges get blockier and may shimmer. Applies the next time the game starts.
Lower caps run cooler and steadier. The cap is rounded to whole refreshes of the screen.

A custom Vulkan driver such as Mesa Turnip makes the game render correctly, and often faster, on Adreno GPUs, where the phone’s own driver can show a black picture.
Custom drivers are for Qualcomm Adreno GPUs. This phone has a different GPU, so the game uses the phone’s own driver.
Needed on this phone: the game shows a black picture with the phone’s own driver. Mesa Turnip is the supported driver.

Percent of the screen per side: higher looks sharper and costs frame rate. Menus and text always stay sharp.

Co-op is experimental for now. It needs its own save that starts from the beginning: your current save cannot be played in co-op, and co-op never uses or changes it.

The card says who hosts. The host presses Play first; the others once the host is in the game.
To host, leave the address empty. To visit, type the host\'s address (for example 192.168.1.20): phones do not find hosts on the network by themselves.
Rooms on the relay show up in Visit a Friend. Leave the public relay, or type your own (IPv4 and port).

Guidance, not a guarantee: tested on the Galaxy Z Fold 6 (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, Adreno 750). The included Mesa Turnip driver lists Adreno 6xx, 7xx and 8xx GPUs (Snapdragon 8 Gen 1 to 8 Gen 3 and 8 Elite). 12 GB of RAM recommended. Phones with other GPUs (Exynos, Mali and others) use their system driver and are untested.

How to get your game files onto the phone
Copy your own dump to this phone
Recompia needs your own decrypted copy of the game, the same folder the PC launcher takes: version 2.0.1a (update 655360), with its exefs and romfs folders. Nothing is downloaded.
Have your dump on a PC
A folder with exefs/ and romfs/, or with base/ and updates/655360/ as the PC launcher accepts it. About 7.3 GB.
About 7.3 GB for the game files, 2.6 GB while the game is built (0.6 GB stay), and 6.6 GB for the shaders. Building the shaders on the phone needs 12 GB free at the start.
Copy the folder to the phone

Connect the phone to the PC with a USB cable, choose File transfer on the phone, and copy the whole folder into the phone’s Download folder. A microSD card or a USB drive works too. Copy in binary mode: a text-mode FTP copy damages the files.

In Game files, a folder in Download or at the top of the phone’s storage is listed under Found on this phone. Otherwise press Choose a folder and pick it. The files are read where they are; nothing is copied.
Optional: bring the shaders from the PC

A Recompia install on a PC has a shader_cache folder. Copy it to Recompia/shader_cache on the phone (/sdcard/Recompia/shader_cache, without its corpus folder): Recompia finds it there and checks it, which saves the long shader translation on the phone.

Free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later (GPL-3.0-or-later).

The Android app uses Jetpack Compose and AndroidX (Apache-2.0), Material Symbols icons (Apache-2.0), the Inter typeface (SIL OFL 1.1), SDL3 (zlib) and libadrenotools (BSD-2-Clause), which loads a GPU driver the player chooses. The touch controls are adapted from the Android touch overlay of Eden (GPL-3.0-or-later). The runtime decodes compressed textures with bcdec (MIT or public domain). The on-device build tools are LLVM clang and lld (Apache-2.0 with LLVM exceptions), Python (PSF License) with capstone (BSD-3-Clause) and lz4 (BSD-2-Clause), and the Android NDK sysroot. Where the app includes the Mesa Turnip driver, it is Mesa (MIT). No other GPU driver is included.
